C0110.d: C0110 does not appear in the accessible J2012 code tables; it is documented by General Motors, whose brake modules use it for the electric motor of the ABS return pump. In the Saab 9-5 (2010–2011) and 9-4X service data the motor sits in the brake pressure modulator valve while its relay is inside the EBCM; the module leaves the motor off during ordinary braking and runs it only for ABS, traction or stability interven
s: ABS and red brake warning lamps on
Traction and stability control indicator on, systems disabled
No ABS intervention on slippery surfaces
c: Open or high-resistance pump motor supply or ground (fuse, connector, ground point)
Seized or worn pump motor in the modulator valve assembly
Faulty pump motor relay inside the brake control module

C0111.d: No accessible J2012 table, manufacturer index or NHTSA bulletin lists C0111, so the code cannot be traced to any published application. The title describes a plausibility monitor rather than a wiring fault: the controller notices that an anti-lock intervention, or one of its pressure-release phases, lasts longer than makes physical sense.
s: ABS warning lamp on, anti-lock function switched off
Pedal pulsing or long release phases during gentle braking
c: Spare wheel, mixed tyre sizes or very uneven tyre pressures
Weak or disturbed wheel speed signal (air gap, dirty sensor ring)
Sluggish valve in the hydraulic unit prolonging a control phase

C0112.d: C0112 is not found in any accessible J2012 table or in the NHTSA bulletin index, and no manufacturer documents it publicly. Read literally, the title flags anti-lock control that starts again and again although the wheel situation does not justify it, as opposed to one overlong event (C0111).
s: ABS kicks in at low speed or on dry road without reason
ABS warning lamp on after repeated interventions
c: Tyre or wheel of the wrong rolling circumference
Cracked, loose or contaminated sensor ring
Interference or intermittent contact on a wheel speed sensor circuit

C0121.d: C0121 is absent from the accessible J2012 lists. GM includes it in the chassis code keyword list of bulletin PIP5094 (2013), and AA1Car's ABS code table, which follows GM numbering, names it Valve Relay Circuit Malfunction.
s: ABS warning lamp on, often together with traction or stability lamp
No anti-lock action, wheels can lock under hard braking
c: Blown fuse or poor battery feed to the valve relay
Corroded or loose ground of the brake control module
Valve relay contact sticking or burnt (relay often inside the module)

C0128.d: C0128 is not part of the accessible J2012 tables. GM lists it among its chassis codes in bulletin PIP5094, and the GM-based ABS table published by AA1Car words it Low Brake Fluid Circuit Low.
s: Red brake warning lamp or low fluid message
Possibly longer pedal travel if fluid is really missing
c: Fluid level genuinely low from pad wear or a leak
Stuck float or shorted reed switch in the reservoir
Chafed switch wiring shorted to ground

C0131.d: C0131 is not in the accessible J2012 lists; GM and Saab use it for the brake pressure sensor that measures master cylinder pressure inside the modulator. In the Saab 9-5 up to 2010 a signal above 4.75 V or under 0.25 V lasting 0.1 s, or a supply outside 4.4–5.6 V, sets it and ABS, TCS and ESP go out of service.
s: Traction/stability control warning on, systems switched off
On some models ABS lamp on as well
c: Brake pressure sensor in the modulator faulty or out of calibration
Shipping material left on the sensor after modulator replacement (GM)
Fault on the 5 V reference or signal circuit of the sensor
Incorrect brake pedal signal used for the plausibility check

C0136.d: No public J2012 list, NHTSA bulletin or manufacturer table carries C0136, so it cannot be matched to a vehicle. Its title is word for word that of C0205, and at GM the brake switch input of ABS/TCS modules is C0161; which number a given car uses can only come from its own service data.
s: Stop lamps stay on or do not work
Cruise control will not engage or cancels
ABS or stability warning lamp may come on
c: Brake light switch misadjusted, worn or sticking
Open or short in the switch circuit or connector

C0141.d: C0141 is not listed in the accessible J2012 tables. Saab documents it for the Bosch 5.3 TC/ABS of the 9-3 and 9-5 from 1998 and for the later 9-5 ESP as the left pressure-increase valve, kept apart from the wheel valve group code C2450; GM's chassis keyword list (PIP5094) includes it, and AA1Car's GM-based table calls it Left TCS Solenoid #1.
s: ABS, brake and central warning lamps on
TCS/ESP off indicator lit, no ABS, TCS or ESP function
c: Open or shorted coil of the left pressure-increase valve
Poor contact between control unit and valve block
Failed valve driver in the control module

C0146.d: Like its neighbours, C0146 is missing from the accessible J2012 tables and is documented only in Saab and GM material. Saab's 9-3/9-5 data for the Bosch 5.3 TC/ABS name it the left pressure-reduction valve, the ESP version of the 9-5 calls it the left pressure relief valve; the GM keyword list PIP5094 includes the number and AA1Car's GM-based table labels it Left TCS Solenoid #2.
s: Several brake-related warning lamps on together
ABS, traction and stability control unavailable
c: Open or shorted coil of the left pressure-reduction valve
Control module fault (Saab replaces the control module after checks)
Weak supply or ground to the brake control unit

C0148.d: C0148 is listed neither in the publicly available J2012 tables nor in maker indexes or NHTSA bulletins, so what the letter B stands for cannot be verified. The title suggests a second release solenoid for the right front wheel, as some hydraulic units pair two valves per channel.
s: ABS warning lamp on immediately after key-on
Anti-lock and related functions switched off
c: Solenoid coil open, shorted or out of resistance range
Corroded contact between coil and control module
Failed output stage in the ABS module

C0151.d: C0151 mirrors C0141 on the right side and, like it, is not in the accessible J2012 tables. Saab's 9-3 and 9-5 workshop pages for the Bosch 5.3 TC/ABS and for the 9-5 ESP define it as the right pressure-increase valve, separate from the right front wheel valve code C2455; GM's PIP5094 keyword list carries it, and AA1Car's GM-based table reads Right TCS Solenoid #1.
s: Brake, ABS and central warning lamps on
No traction control when a front wheel spins
c: Defective coil of the right pressure-increase valve
Contact fault at the module-to-valve-block interface
Valve driver fault in the brake control module

C0153.d: C0153 cannot be found in any accessible J2012 list, NHTSA bulletin or manufacturer table; neither the code nor its B suffix is publicly documented. By title it concerns a second inlet solenoid for the right front wheel.
s: ABS lamp on, anti-lock unavailable
Stability control may also be switched off
c: Poor plug contact between coil and module
Internal fault in the ABS control module

C0156.d: C0156 completes the Saab/GM group of four and is likewise absent from the accessible J2012 tables. Saab lists it as the right pressure-reduction valve for the 9-3/9-5 with Bosch 5.3 traction control and as the right pressure relief valve in the 9-5 ESP; GM's PIP5094 keyword list names the code, and AA1Car's GM-based table gives Right TCS Solenoid #2.
s: ABS, brake and TCS/ESP OFF lamps on
Wheels may lock under emergency braking
c: Open or shorted coil of the right pressure-reduction valve
Fault inside the control unit carrying the valve coils
Moisture or corrosion at the control unit connector

C0158.d: C0158 is publicly undocumented: it appears in no accessible J2012 table, NHTSA bulletin or manufacturer index. Saab, for example, reports the rear left valve group under C2415 instead.
s: ABS warning lamp on, anti-lock switched off
Rear wheels can lock under hard braking
c: Rear left inlet coil open, shorted or with wrong resistance
Corrosion at the hydraulic unit connector
Failed output stage in the control module

C0161.d: C0161 is outside the accessible J2012 tables but well documented at GM. Service data for the later Saab 9-5 and the 9-4X define it as an implausible ABS brake switch signal: the EBCM receives the pedal-applied message from the body module and compares it with brake pressure and vehicle motion.
s: Service stability or traction message
Cruise control or brake lights may misbehave
Hill start assist unavailable
c: Brake pedal position sensor or switch out of adjustment
Loose or backed-out terminal in the pedal sensor wiring (GM X205)
Brake pressure sensor reading that contradicts the pedal signal

C0163.d: None of the reachable J2012 lists, maker indexes or NHTSA bulletins mention C0163, so its use cannot be shown for any vehicle. The title names the outlet solenoid of the left rear brake, the valve that opens during anti-lock control to dump caliper pressure toward the return pump and lets the wheel recover.
s: ABS warning lamp on
Unstable rear axle under hard braking without ABS
c: Rear left outlet coil open or shorted
Outlet valve mechanically stuck by contaminated fluid
Poor contact at the hydraulic unit connector

C0168.d: C0168 has no public trace: it is missing from the accessible J2012 tables, from the NHTSA bulletin index and from the manufacturer pages checked, where Saab for instance uses C2485 for the rear right valves. Taken at face value it covers the inlet solenoid of the right rear brake, which isolates that caliper from master cylinder pressure while the module regulates the wheel.
s: ABS lamp on, often directly at key-on
No anti-lock control on any wheel
c: Open winding in the rear right inlet coil
Corroded plug at the valve block

C0173.d: No accessible J2012 list, maker index or NHTSA bulletin contains C0173, so the code cannot be tied to any vehicle; Saab, for instance, reports a fault in either valve of the right rear wheel as C2485. By its title it covers the release valve of the right rear brake.
s: ABS and brake warning lamps on, ABS/TCS/ESC switched off
Right rear wheel may lock under hard braking
c: Open or shorted coil of the right rear outlet valve
Corroded or loose contact between valve block and control module
Faulty valve driver stage inside the control module

C0185.d: C0185 is missing from the accessible J2012 lists and from the NHTSA bulletin index, and no maker documents it, so it is not publicly verifiable; its title is shared with C0499. It describes a lateral acceleration signal that is electrically intact but does not fit the motion of the car.
s: Stability control warning lamp on, ESC switched off
Unwanted stability interventions when cornering
c: Sensor offset drifted or calibration not learned after replacement
Sensor or module loose or mounted at the wrong angle
Implausible comparison signal (steering angle, wheel speeds)

C0186.d: C0186 lies outside the publicly available J2012 tables but is firmly established at GM and Saab for the lateral accelerometer. On Saab 9-5 models through 2010 the ESP module sets it when the 0–5 V signal leaves the 0.25–4.75 V band for over 0.1 s or makes no sense; at standstill the reading should be close to 0 m/s².
s: Service StabiliTrak / ESP OFF message or lamp
Traction and stability control unavailable
Further chassis codes (C0196, C0287, U-codes) stored
c: Corroded connector or terminals in the sensor or bus wiring
Outdated software in the module that hosts the sensor (e.g. airbag module)

C0196.d: C0196 is absent from the accessible J2012 lists, yet it is the yaw rate code of GM and Saab and is also used by Karma. The Saab 9-5 sets it when the sensor output leaves 0.25–4.75 V for longer than 0.1 s or its 2.1–2.9 V reference strays for 0.2 s; GM's multi-axis sensor reports 00 for a faulty signal and 5A when offset or plausibility against lateral acceleration, steering angle and speed fail.
s: Service StabiliTrak message, traction/ABS or ESP OFF lamp
Stability control and hill start assist disabled
Red brake lamp on in some vehicles
c: Code set during transport or flat towing while modules were awake
Faulty or unlearned yaw rate / multi-axis sensor
Signal spikes from body vibration, stone impacts or loose mounting
Corroded connector or CAN wiring fault
